title: He rose.
paragraphs: “Peter replied, ‘Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.’” — Acts 2:38

The resurrection is not just proof that Jesus is alive.
It is a demand on your life.

Because if the tomb is empty, then your excuses are empty too.
Your hiding place is gone.
Your secret sin is exposed in the light of a living Christ.

That was the moment in Acts 2.
Peter did not preach a soft message to a comfortable crowd.
He preached Christ crucified.
Christ risen.
Christ exalted.
And the people were cut to the heart.

That is what real resurrection preaching does.
It does not entertain your flesh.
It confronts your rebellion.
It calls for a response.

Repent.
Turn around.
Drop the mask.
Stop defending what nailed Jesus to the cross.

Be baptized.
Go public with your surrender.
Let your life declare, “I belong to Jesus now.”

But here’s what we miss:
Acts 2:38 is not a threat hanging over your head.
It is mercy with the door still open.

The same Jesus you offended is the Jesus who offers forgiveness.
The same Savior you resisted is the Savior who receives the broken.
The same risen King who convicts you is the King who fills you with His Spirit.

This is the Gospel.
Not behavior management.
Not religious performance.
A crucified and risen Christ calling sinners home.

Not tomorrow.
Not when life settles down.
Not when you feel cleaner.

Repent.
Believe the risen Jesus.
Step into the grace His blood purchased and His resurrection secured.

Because the resurrection is not only something to celebrate.
It is something to answer.
